title: Seoul police refer Gangnam plastic surgery clinic director and ad agency staff over fake reviews posted from hacked portal accounts
date_note: The page gives only its publication day; the date is the day it was published.
geo_basis: Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency Cyber Investigation Division, named by the source; pin at Seoul
summary: Herald Business reports that the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's cyber investigation division referred the director of a Gangnam plastic surgery clinic and advertising agency staff to prosecutors under the Medical Service Act and the Information and Communications Network Act. Police say hacked portal accounts bought from a Chinese hacking group were used to post fake reviews and comments. Police say they asked portals to delete the fake posts they identified.
plain: Seoul police say a clinic and its ad staff used hacked portal accounts to post fake patient reviews, and have referred them to prosecutors, according to Herald Business.
exec: Police say hacked accounts fuel paid fake reviews, a fraud that misleads customers choosing a clinic.
impact: Fake reviews posted on portal cafes and beauty-medical information platforms, per the article.

validation.note: One publisher read (Herald Business), quoting the police; the police's own release was not read.

review.note: stronger than source: plan to ask portals to delete now asked portals; date, laws, Chinese group checked against Herald Business
